comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> When using mini.completion with mini.snippets, snippets are not proposed in markdown buffers with marksman LSP. They still trigger after a '#' character. I don't know if it is a mini.nvim bug or a marksman bug.

I don't fully understand the problem and can not reproduce. Could you please elaborate:
- What keys are pressed that you expect to show snippets but there is none?
- Which snippets do you expect to be shown: the ones loaded with 'mini.snippets' (i.e. from 'global.json' and 'markdown' language of 'rafamadriz/friendly-snippets') or the ones provided by `marksman` LSP server (not sure which ones would that be)? I can see 'mini.snippets' snippets both after `<C-Space>` (force completion) and typing `#`.

Couple of notes:
- Typing `#` leads to automatic show of completion menu because `#` character is configured as trigger character for `marksman` LSP server. However, it is not involved into matching/filtering of candidates (i.e. not recognized as "base") because 'mini.completion' does not recognize it as part of keyword. All while `marksman` doesn't seem to provide additional information about how it computes its base.
- Using `MiniSnippets.start_lsp_server({ match = false })` results into 'mini.completion' taking care of matching/filtering of candidate snippets provided by 'mini.snippets'. This can be both a good thing or a bad thing. For example, `match = false` will not recognize snippet prefixes that start with `#` while default (i.e. `match = true`) will have 'mini.snippets' itself recognize those.

I'd like to have friendly-snippets in the completion box.

I've notice this in lsp.log : 
```
[ERROR][2025-06-03 12:05:23] ...p/_transport.lua:36	"rpc"	"marksman"	"stderr"	"[12:05:23 INF] <LSP Entry> Starting Marksman LSP server: {}\n"
[ERROR][2025-06-03 12:05:23] ...p/_transport.lua:36	"rpc"	"marksman"	"stderr"	'[12:05:23 INF] <Folder> Loading folder documents: {"uri": "file:///Users/bcarnazzi/notes"}\n'
[START][2025-06-03 12:06:22] LSP logging initiated

[WARN][2025-06-03 12:06:22] .../lua/vim/lsp.lua:439	"mini.snippets does not have a configuration"
```

When I type C-Space after, for example word "bold", nothing happens (that should trigger a snippet completion).
Doesn't work with tab key either.

Note : I use nvim-lspconfig with the default marksman configuration : 

```
---@brief
---
--- https://github.com/artempyanykh/marksman
---
--- Marksman is a Markdown LSP server providing completion, cross-references, diagnostics, and more.
---
--- Marksman works on MacOS, Linux, and Windows and is distributed as a self-contained binary for each OS.
---
--- Pre-built binaries can be downloaded from https://github.com/artempyanykh/marksman/releases

local bin_name = 'marksman'
local cmd = { bin_name, 'server' }

return {
  cmd = cmd,
  filetypes = { 'markdown', 'markdown.mdx' },
  root_markers = { '.marksman.toml', '.git' },
}
```

> When I type C-Space after, for example word "bold", nothing happens (that should trigger a snippet completion).
> Doesn't work with tab key either.

Aha, I see. I indeed could reproduce. For me it also didn't expand snippets with 'mini.snippets' directly (like after `<C-j>`) and showed that there is no matching snippets for `'markdown_inline'` language.

So the core issue here is how tree-sitter works in markdown: it is not one parser with language `markdown`, but two parsers `markdown` and `markdown_inline`. I am not sure about details of why this is needed, but I am sure there are reasons.

To overcome this, adjusting [language patterns of how 'mini.snippets' works with markdown](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/e32271c87c02ae0a875c5ea7942081318a075969/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L825-L833) worked for me. So could you please replace `gen_loader.from_lang()` in the original setup with the `gen_loader.from_lang({ lang_patterns = { markdown_inline = { 'markdown.json' } } })` and see it that fixes the issue? This will instruct 'mini.snippets' to search for file 'snippets/markdown.json' (which is where 'friendly-snippets' stores snippets for markdown language) when trying to compute relevant snippets for `markdown_inline` language.
Great! Thanks for confirming! I'll add this to the documentation also then.
My guess is that markdown_inline is for syntax highlighting for embedded markdown sections in other file formats

> My guess is that markdown_inline is for syntax highlighting for embedded markdown sections in other file formats

Maybe, but at least not only. It is at least for stuff like inline links, bold/italic text, etc.

title: [mini.completion] snippets are not proposed in markdown buffers with Marksman LSP
